explanation: Eye contact in Singapore generally signals confidence and attentiveness, similar to Western norms, but prolonged or intense eye contact can come across as challenging or confrontational, especially with someone senior. Some Malay Muslims and Hindus may lower or avert their eyes more when speaking with elders or superiors as a sign of respect, not disinterest.
local_tip: Keep eye contact natural and intermittent, especially with older or more senior people; don't read a lowered gaze from a Malay or Indian colleague as disengagement.
regional_note: Muslim Malay and some Hindu Singaporeans may avert their eyes more often with superiors or elders as a mark of deference; this is a sign of respect, not avoidance or dishonesty.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can feel confrontational; brief, intermittent eye contact is preferred, especially with seniors.
Steady eye contact is expected and read as a sign of confidence and honesty.
Lowering the eyes with elders or superiors is a sign of respect rather than dishonesty or disinterest.
